question: When approaching a junction and the traffic lights signal change from green to amber, you should

options.text: Stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Stop only if a red light camera is in use.

question: The signal given by the Policeman in the picture means
picture: Traffic policeman in white uniform, helmet and gloves, facing forward with both arms down at his sides

options.text: Vehicles approaching from his left and right to stop.
Vehicles approaching from in front and behind him to stop.
Vehicles approaching from all directions to stop.

question: Which of these driver's arm signal mean he intends to move in or turn left?

options.text: Rear view of a car on a lighter red background, driver's arm at right window, no motion lines
Rear view of a car, driver's arm out of right window with a large orange oval motion loop
Rear view of a car, driver's arm out of right window with small orange stacked motion marks

notes: Option pictures are tiny, low-resolution thumbnails (probably stills of animated arm signals); fine detail is hard to make out.

question: Which of these driver's arm signal indicates that he intends to stop?

options.text: Rear view of a car, driver's arm out of right window with a large orange oval motion loop
Rear view of a car, driver's arm out of right window with small orange stacked motion marks
Rear view of a car on a lighter red background, driver's arm at right window, no motion lines

notes: Option pictures are tiny, low-resolution thumbnails (probably stills of animated arm signals); fine detail is hard to make out. Same three pictures as Q23 in a different order.

question: If the car you are overtaking is drifting in its lane, you should

options.text: Use your horn to warn him.
Signal him with your hand.
Overtake it quickly.

question: To drive in a way where other drivers will not find it necessary to overtake you, you should

options.text: Drive on the extreme right lane all the time.
Always drive at a speed that match the traffic flow.
Drive at the maximun speed limit of the road all the time.

notes: Source typo in option C: 'maximun' (for 'maximum'). Option B reads 'match' as printed.

question: Which car has the right of way?
picture: Video frame from above: roundabout at a crossroads, blue car A on the roundabout, orange car M approaching from below, roundabout sign on the left

options.text: Car A.
Car M.
Either car A or M.

question: In traffic hold-ups, you should

options.text: Try to get ahead of others by overtaking them on the right.
Try to get ahead of others by overtaking them on the left.
Stay in queue and follow the traffic flow.

question: When you see a vehicle slowing down before a Zebra Crossing, you should

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Sound the horn before passing the slow moving vehicle.
Maintain your speed.

question: Road hogging

options.text: Allows others to overtake safely.
Holds up the flow of traffic.
Reduces road accident.

question: You want to reverse into a side road. You are not sure that the area behind your vehicle is clear. What should you do?

options.text: Carry on, assuming it is clear.
Look through the rear window only.
Get out and check.

question: Before entering a round about, you should

options.text: Give way to traffic on your right.
Stop first before entering.
Accelerate to merge smoothly with traffic already in the roundabout.

notes: Question prints 'round about' as two words; option C prints 'roundabout'.

question: Before moving off, you should

options.text: Use your mirrors and signal if necessary.
Use your mirrors, check your blind spot and signal.
Signal and move.

question: Drinking and driving may cause

options.text: Increase confidence.
Loss of proper control of the vehicle.
Greater awareness of danger.

question: Generally a small amount of alcohol can make you less safe on the road.

options.text: True.
False.
Not true, if you were an experience driver.

notes: Source typo in option C: 'experience driver' (for 'experienced').

question: How does the consumption of alcohol affect a person's driving ?

options.text: It enables the driver to make better judgements.
It enables the driver to have better vision of the road.
It reduces the driver's reaction.

notes: Question has a space before the question mark, as printed.

question: In this scenario Car A should
picture: Video frame from above: blue car A behind a lorry on a road, near a side road junction on the lorry's left

options.text: Quickly overtake the lorry before the junction.
Slow down and let the lorry complete the turn.
Overtake the lorry on the left.

question: Which car (X or Y) should exit at points C and D?
picture: Video frame from above: roundabout with exits labelled A, B, C, D; blue car X and yellow car Y side by side entering from below

options.text: Car X.
Car Y.
Both vehicles.

question: 'Blind spots' of a vehicle is an area which cannot be viewed by

options.text: The rear view mirror.
Left and right wings mirrors.
Both A and B.

question: The Two-second Rule is a simple check to ensure

options.text: A safe distance for you to move off from a junction.
A safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.
A safe length of time to signal before your manoeuvre.
